name: Latitude Bands
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web dashboard composition study, 16:10 landscape viewport
Primary request: Design a sophisticated Hyperion service dashboard named Hyperion using the approved Service Atlas visual system. This is a designed web interface, not a poster or physical scene.
Structure: no permanent left sidebar. Use a slim top bar with brand, global search, and three labeled destinations. Below, organize all services into three wide horizontal atlas bands such as Production, Workshop, and Archive, each with a coordinate label in the left margin and a shared ruled list across the page. The currently selected service expands inline inside its band into a compact dossier with a clear Open service action; a narrow vertical bearings strip on the right summarizes reachable, slow, paused, and down counts. Logs appear as a collapsible bottom drawer hint, not a main panel. Prioritize recognition and direct access.
Style/medium: refined production-grade SaaS UI mockup, cartographic editorial precision, flat semantic interface.
Color palette: warm mineral ivory #F4F0E6, parchment #FBF8F0, limestone #E4DDCF, carbon #282824, graphite #615F57, rare aged brass #876721, restrained green/ochre/red service states. Gold occupies less than ten percent.
Materials/textures: matte paper and engraved wayfinding implied only through tone, hairline rules, coordinate alignment, and tiny plotted bearings; no literal paper texture.
Typography: distinctive compact contemporary grotesk with a subtly human technical display voice; clear workspace title and disciplined small labels.
Text verbatim: Hyperion and Your deployed world, within reach.
Constraints: direct open-service actions must be obvious; status never uses gold; accessibility-conscious contrast; show illustrative service entries without real-company claims.
Avoid: Greek letters, blue, columns, laurels, temples, amphorae, parchment cosplay, ornamental mythology, generic card grid, glassmorphism, gradients, neon, excessive gold, dark mode, poster composition, photorealism, device frame, watermark.
